semantic_correction.stem: Two hours after a thyroidectomy, a client develops rapidly increasing anterior neck swelling, inspiratory stridor, dyspnea, and an oxygen saturation of 88%. Which action by the RN is most appropriate?

options.A: Apply a cold pack to the neck swelling, keep the client supine, and reassess respiratory status after the swelling has had time to decrease.
options.B: Activate the emergency response, stay with the client, support oxygenation, and urgently summon the surgical/airway team for possible airway compromise.
options.C: Obtain a serum calcium level and assess for Chvostek and Trousseau signs before escalating because postoperative stridor most often reflects hypocalcemia.
options.D: Encourage voice rest, elevate oral fluid intake, and notify the surgeon during routine rounds because hoarseness and neck swelling are expected after surgery.

semantic_correction.rationale: The 2026 NCSBN NCLEX-RN Test Plan explicitly includes postoperative care, recognition and intervention for client complications, and emergency-care procedures under Physiological Adaptation. Current StatPearls thyroidectomy guidance identifies postoperative hemorrhage and rapidly expanding neck hematoma as potentially life-threatening because they can compromise the airway and require urgent intervention. Current Open RN endocrine guidance lists dyspnea, neck swelling, stridor and low oxygen levels as findings of post-thyroidectomy airway compromise that require immediate respiratory monitoring and emergency readiness. This client has multiple signs of active upper-airway compromise and hypoxemia. B is therefore the uniquely best response: summon emergency surgical/airway help immediately while staying with the client and supporting oxygenation. A delays definitive response. C prioritizes a possible metabolic complication despite overt airway obstruction signs. D treats the findings as routine postoperative changes and delays emergency management. Therefore B is correct.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: After thyroidectomy, rapidly increasing neck swelling with stridor, dyspnea and hypoxemia is an airway emergency; immediately activate emergency assistance, remain with the client, support oxygenation and obtain urgent surgical/airway intervention rather than delaying for routine reassessment or laboratory evaluation.

semantic_correction.source_locator: StatPearls Thyroidectomy > Complications — postoperative hemorrhage/hematoma can rapidly cause airway compromise and may require urgent evacuation/emergency airway management. Open RN Health Alterations Table 7.6c — post-thyroidectomy airway compromise findings include difficulty breathing, neck swelling, stridor, low oxygen levels and require respiratory monitoring/emergency readiness. NCSBN Physiological Adaptation — provide postoperative care; recognize signs/symptoms of complications and intervene; perform emergency care procedures.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: retired bedside-shift-report benefit recall because it overlapped existing handoff coverage and had a strong key-length cue. Rebuilt the item around an explicit NCSBN postoperative/emergency-care construct: recognition and escalation of post-thyroidectomy airway compromise. Removed the prior absolute-word and answer-length cues.

audit_findings_append.finding: The replacement tests immediate recognition and escalation of a life-threatening postoperative airway complication.
audit_findings_append.source_authority: StatPearls Thyroidectomy; Open RN; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan

scope_exclusions.specific_cause_of_airway_compromise: The item does not require distinguishing hematoma, edema, nerve injury or hypocalcemic tetany before responding; the presented airway compromise requires immediate escalation.
scope_exclusions.bedside_wound_opening_by_RN: Not endorsed. Definitive wound/airway intervention is performed by the appropriate emergency surgical/airway team according to the clinical situation and institutional protocol.
scope_exclusions.routine_hoarseness: Not tested; the stem contains stridor, progressive neck swelling, dyspnea and hypoxemia, which are not routine findings.

near_duplicate_check.note: Q0724 tests generic postoperative deterioration meeting rapid-response criteria; Q0874 tests abdominal evisceration; Q0875 tracheostomy secretion clearance. Q0920 specifically tests upper-airway compromise after thyroidectomy. Targeted repository search returned no matching thyroidectomy/stridor/neck-hematoma item before staging.

option_audit.A: Plausible swelling-management response but dangerously delays an established airway emergency.
option_audit.B: Correct. It prioritizes emergency airway support and immediate surgical/airway-team response.
option_audit.C: Plausible post-thyroidectomy hypocalcemia assessment but delays management of overt airway compromise.
option_audit.D: Plausible response to benign postoperative voice changes but misclassifies severe airway signs as expected recovery.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer. Stridor, progressive neck swelling, dyspnea and SpO2 88% establish an immediate airway threat. B alone escalates and supports the airway without delay; A/C/D postpone emergency intervention.

cueing_check.note: All options are comparable action sequences; correct B is not the longest and is close in length to C/D.

blueprint_audit.entry_level_relevance: Postoperative care, recognition/intervention for complications, and emergency-care procedures are explicit Physiological Adaptation responsibilities.
blueprint_audit.visual_verification: The official NCSBN Physiological Adaptation overview page was visually verified in this audit sequence; a screenshot attempt of the later medical-emergency page failed with a cache-miss error, which is documented rather than presented as a successful screenshot.
